meta.label: AI assistants
meta.attribution: Built from public policies, model and system cards, regulator decisions and open-weight releases, not measured data. AI policies change fast, so verify current settings yourself. Privacy reflects whether the consumer product trains on your chats by default; openness reflects whether the weights can actually be downloaded and run under a licence that says so, not whether a company calls a product open. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare AI assistants by privacy, everyday access, disclosure, and openness.

axes.label: Access or privacy
axes.question: Easier access or less data exposure?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Local / open models (Ollama, llama.cpp)
products.description: A local-first route that keeps prompts on your own machine when you run open-weight models yourself.

privacy.note: A local runtime can keep prompts on-device; privacy then depends on your model, plugins and update settings.

transparency.note: The runtime stack is inspectable, but model transparency varies widely by the weights you choose.

openness.note: llama.cpp and many compatible GGUF models are built for local open-weight inference.

safety.note: Local runtimes usually leave guardrails, filters and policy enforcement to the user or app wrapper.

accessibility.note: Ollama makes local setup easier, but users still need enough hardware and some installation comfort.

products.name: Jan
products.description: An open-source desktop assistant for running local models, with optional cloud-provider connections when you choose them.

privacy.note: Jan says local use stores conversations and usage logs locally, while remote API use sends data to the chosen provider.

transparency.note: Jan is built in public, with an active public GitHub repository and docs for local models and cloud integrations.

openness.note: The Jan repository describes it as an open-source ChatGPT replacement that runs offline and is licensed under Apache 2.0.

safety.note: Local Jan deployments inherit safety behavior from the chosen model and user configuration rather than a single managed safety program.

accessibility.note: Jan offers desktop downloads and a polished UI, but local model performance still depends on hardware and model setup.

products.name: LM Studio
products.description: A polished desktop app for finding, downloading, and running local LLMs with minimal telemetry by default.

privacy.note: LM Studio's app privacy policy says messages, chat histories, and documents are saved locally by default and not transmitted.

transparency.note: LM Studio documents limited update/model-search data flows, but the desktop app itself is proprietary software.

openness.note: LM Studio can run open models locally, but its terms treat the app source code as proprietary and confidential.

safety.note: The app works with third-party AI models, leaving model safety and license compliance largely to user choice.

accessibility.note: LM Studio provides a consumer-friendly desktop app and model search/download flow, but useful models still need capable hardware.

products.name: Open WebUI
products.description: A self-hosted web interface for local and OpenAI-compatible models, strongest for people comfortable running their own server.

privacy.note: Open WebUI is designed as a self-hosted platform that can operate entirely offline when paired with local model runners.

transparency.note: Open WebUI has public docs and a public GitHub repository, making deployment and feature behavior inspectable.

openness.note: Open WebUI is source-available/open development, though its current license includes Open WebUI branding-preservation requirements.

safety.note: Safety depends on the configured model, tools, permissions, and admin setup rather than a single managed model safety stack.

accessibility.note: It is powerful and mobile-friendly after setup, but Docker/server administration makes it less approachable than hosted chat apps.

products.name: Lumo by Proton
products.description: A privacy-first AI assistant from Proton, strongest for people who want hosted chat without ad profiling or default training on conversations.

privacy.note: Proton says Lumo uses zero-access encryption for saved chats, keeps no logs, and does not use conversations to train AI models.

transparency.note: Proton publishes Lumo privacy details and product limits, though the underlying hosted models are not documented like open-weight releases.

openness.note: Lumo is a hosted Proton service rather than a self-hostable model, so the privacy posture is strong but the weights are not open.

safety.note: Lumo inherits managed-model safety controls, but Proton's public materials emphasize privacy more than detailed model or system-card reporting.

accessibility.note: Lumo is available on the web and mobile apps with a free path, making it easier to use than self-hosted private AI stacks.

products.name: Apple Intelligence
products.description: Apple's system-level AI layer for newer iPhone, iPad and Mac devices, best for people already in the Apple ecosystem.

privacy.note: Apple describes an on-device-first design with Private Cloud Compute for larger requests and limits on server-side retention and access.

transparency.note: Apple publishes a technical Private Cloud Compute security model, giving more detail than most closed consumer AI assistants.

openness.note: Apple Intelligence is a closed, device-and-cloud feature layer with no self-hostable weights or open-source assistant stack.

safety.note: Apple limits supported features, devices, and cloud compute paths, but public model-card style reporting is less extensive than open AI model releases.

accessibility.note: The feature is integrated into Apple devices but limited to supported hardware, OS versions, regions and languages.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy AI
products.description: Samsung's AI feature suite for Galaxy devices, useful for mainstream mobile users who want AI built into phone workflows.

privacy.note: Samsung describes both on-device and cloud Galaxy AI processing, with some controls for limiting cloud-dependent processing.

transparency.note: Samsung publishes Galaxy AI feature pages and Knox admin controls, but model and provider detail is still less inspectable than open systems.

openness.note: Galaxy AI is a closed device-and-cloud feature layer rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Knox enterprise controls can restrict some Galaxy AI data processing, but safety still depends on Samsung's closed implementation and cloud partners.

accessibility.note: Galaxy AI is built into recent Samsung devices, making it mainstream but still hardware- and region-dependent.

products.name: Amazon Q Developer
products.description: AWS's coding and cloud assistant, strongest for developers already working in AWS, IDEs, terminals and enterprise controls.

privacy.note: AWS documents encryption and data-protection practices for Amazon Q Developer, with separate controls for service-improvement data use.

transparency.note: Amazon Q Developer has detailed AWS documentation for data protection, opt-out behavior, pricing and integration surfaces.

openness.note: Amazon Q Developer is a closed AWS service with no self-hostable assistant weights.

safety.note: AWS provides enterprise security controls, but generated code and cloud actions still require developer review and permission design.

accessibility.note: Amazon Q Developer offers free and paid tiers across IDE, CLI and AWS workflows, especially accessible to AWS users.

products.name: Replit Agent
products.description: A web-based app-building agent that turns prompts into projects, most useful for learners, prototypes and small web apps.

privacy.note: Replit's general privacy policy covers broad collection and use of service data; Agent docs do not present a narrow no-training privacy posture.

transparency.note: Replit documents Agent behavior, checkpoints and pricing, but the hosted agent and model stack remain closed.

openness.note: Replit Agent is a closed hosted service rather than a self-hostable agent.

safety.note: Replit provides checkpoints, rollback and a Project Security Center, but autonomous code generation can still make destructive or insecure changes.

accessibility.note: Replit offers browser-based building and daily Agent credits on the Starter plan, giving it unusually low setup friction.

products.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
products.description: An AI assistant built into JetBrains IDEs, strongest for developers who already use the JetBrains toolchain.

privacy.note: JetBrains says detailed code-related AI data collection is opt-in, with additional consent safeguards for commercial users.

transparency.note: JetBrains publishes separate data-handling, product-data collection, terms and plan documentation for its AI service.

openness.note: The assistant is a closed JetBrains service integrated into proprietary IDEs, though some workflows can connect to different providers.

safety.note: JetBrains documents data handling and IDE integration, but generated code and agentic actions still need ordinary developer review.

accessibility.note: JetBrains offers AI Free, Pro and Ultimate plan structures, but practical access usually assumes a supported JetBrains IDE workflow.

products.name: Tabnine
products.description: A code assistant oriented around privacy, enterprise deployment choices and IDE autocomplete/chat workflows.

privacy.note: Tabnine states a no-train-no-retain posture for code, with SaaS, VPC, on-prem and air-gapped deployment options.

transparency.note: Tabnine publishes code-privacy and privacy documentation that directly describes retention, training and deployment options.

openness.note: Tabnine is a closed commercial assistant even though it supports private deployment patterns.

safety.note: Tabnine's controls are strong for IP/privacy risk, but code suggestions and AI changes still need developer review and tests.

accessibility.note: Tabnine integrates with common IDEs, but the strongest privacy and deployment guarantees are more enterprise-oriented.

products.name: Amp by Sourcegraph
products.description: A terminal/editor coding agent designed for high-autonomy software work, strongest for experienced developers and teams.

privacy.note: Amp's security reference says the cloud service stores thread data and partial code context, while enterprise workspaces can get zero data retention and no training.

transparency.note: Amp publishes a detailed owner manual, privacy policy, security reference and model/provider documentation.

openness.note: Amp is not self-hosted and uses hosted model providers, though it exposes local CLI/editor workflows and some provider configuration.

safety.note: Amp documents permissions, secret redaction and prompt-injection defenses, but high-autonomy coding agents still carry meaningful execution risk.

accessibility.note: Amp runs in terminal and editor workflows, which is powerful for developers but less approachable than browser-first chat assistants.

products.name: Devin
products.description: A high-autonomy software engineering agent from Cognition, aimed more at professional teams than casual AI chat users.

privacy.note: Devin documents isolated ephemeral sandboxes, scoped credentials and secret redaction, while still operating as a closed hosted service.

transparency.note: Cognition publishes security, privacy and compliance documentation, including SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 claims.

openness.note: Devin is a closed commercial coding agent with no open weights or self-hostable public stack.

safety.note: Devin's security model includes sandbox isolation and credential controls, but its high-autonomy coding workflows require careful review and permissions.

accessibility.note: Devin is aimed at paid professional and team workflows, so consumer accessibility is much lower than free chat assistants.

products.name: Devin Desktop (Windsurf)
products.description: The renamed Windsurf IDE, now positioned by Cognition as a desktop command center for local and cloud coding agents.

privacy.note: Cognition's privacy policy covers Devin and Windsurf, collects user content, and says content may be used to improve or train models depending on applicable terms.

transparency.note: Cognition announced Devin Desktop as the next generation of Windsurf and documents the IDE, Cascade, local agent and agent-management workflows.

openness.note: Devin Desktop supports ACP-compatible agents, but the IDE and bundled agent experience are a closed commercial product.

safety.note: Cascade includes code mode, tool calling, terminal access and checkpoints, so safety depends on permissions, review habits and rollback discipline.

accessibility.note: Devin Desktop is documented for Mac, Windows and Linux, supports free signup, and can import VS Code or Cursor settings.

products.name: LibreChat
products.description: An open-source, self-hosted chat interface that connects to many model providers and can keep conversation storage under your control.

privacy.note: LibreChat can be self-hosted and store conversations in your own database, while requests still follow the policies of whichever model provider you connect.

transparency.note: LibreChat is developed in a public GitHub repository with public docs and deployment configuration.

openness.note: LibreChat is an open-source, self-hostable interface, though model openness depends on the connected provider or local model.

safety.note: Safety depends on the chosen model, tools, plugins and admin configuration rather than a single managed assistant safety system.

accessibility.note: LibreChat is free and flexible, but self-hosting, model keys and admin setup make it less accessible than hosted consumer assistants.

products.name: AnythingLLM
products.description: A local-first and self-hostable AI workspace for private chat, documents, RAG and agents with local or cloud models.

privacy.note: AnythingLLM emphasizes private local and self-hosted deployment paths, with privacy depending on whether you use local or cloud model providers.

transparency.note: AnythingLLM has public docs and a public repository describing desktop, Docker and provider configuration.

openness.note: AnythingLLM is open source and self-hostable, while model openness varies by the local or cloud model a user connects.

safety.note: Safety depends on configured models, agents, document permissions and workspace administration rather than a managed public safety layer.

accessibility.note: Desktop and Docker options make private setup more approachable than many self-hosted AI stacks, but it still requires model/provider choices.

products.name: GPT4All
products.description: A local desktop AI app for running private local models, strongest for people who want offline chat without API calls.

privacy.note: GPT4All is presented as a private local desktop chatbot that can run models on-device without API calls.

transparency.note: GPT4All is developed in a public repository with inspectable desktop app and local model tooling.

openness.note: GPT4All is open source and supports local models, though individual model weights and licenses vary.

safety.note: Running local models improves privacy but leaves model choice, moderation, updates and safety boundaries mostly to the user.

accessibility.note: GPT4All offers desktop apps and local inference paths that do not require an API key or dedicated GPU for common use.

products.name: Duck.ai
products.description: A privacy-first AI chat front end that routes to major models without an account or retained chat history.

privacy.note: DuckDuckGo says it strips identifying metadata such as IP address before sending a prompt to a model provider, that no provider may use Duck.ai conversations to train models, and that providers apply Zero Data Retention, deleting prompts and responses immediately after replying, with a documented exception letting OpenAI and Anthropic hold data in memory for up to one hour for prompt caching.

transparency.note: Duck.ai documents provider limits, local/encrypted chat-history options and a zero-provider-visibility path for supported models.

openness.note: Duck.ai routes to several models, including some open-weight options, but the router itself is not self-hostable.

safety.note: Safety mainly inherits from the selected provider model rather than a separate public Duck.ai safety framework.

accessibility.note: Duck.ai is available in browser with no account, and privacy terms describe free private chat access.

products.name: Brave Leo
products.description: A browser-integrated assistant designed around local chat history and no account requirement.

privacy.note: Brave says Leo does not retain or share chats, does not use them for additional model training, and requires no account or login.

transparency.note: Brave documents Leo's privacy posture and model choices, though provider behavior still depends on the selected model path.

openness.note: Leo is a Brave product using selected providers/models, not a self-hosted open-weight assistant.

safety.note: Leo mostly depends on chosen model safeguards rather than a standalone public frontier-safety framework.

accessibility.note: Leo is built into Brave with free use and paid premium options, making it easy for Brave users.

products.name: Claude (Anthropic)
products.description: A frontier assistant with unusually strong safety documentation, but consumer training settings now require closer attention.

privacy.note: Anthropic says Claude Free, Pro and Max do not train on chats by default; chats are used to improve Claude only if a user opts in through Privacy Settings, and Incognito chats stay excluded from training even when that setting is on.

transparency.note: Anthropic publishes model system cards and a dedicated transparency hub for deployed Claude models.

openness.note: Claude model weights are closed; public disclosure is via system cards and policies rather than downloadable weights.

safety.note: Anthropic maintains a public Responsible Scaling Policy and updates it as frontier-risk thresholds change.

accessibility.note: Claude has free and paid consumer tiers, but high-use access is gated by subscription and usage limits.

products.name: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
products.description: The most mainstream AI assistant: highly accessible, improving transparency, but consumer training controls still matter.

privacy.note: OpenAI's Data Controls FAQ lets users turn off model improvement for the consumer service; Temporary Chats are not used for training, do not create memories and are deleted after 30 days.

transparency.note: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 August Update system card reports safety and capability evaluations for the Sol and Luna tiers, covering disallowed-content testing, jailbreak and prompt-injection resistance, and factuality checks, and states both tiers earned Preparedness Framework 'High' capability ratings for biological/chemical and cybersecurity risk.

openness.note: ChatGPT's served frontier models remain closed. OpenAI separately publishes gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b under an Apache 2.0 licence, downloadable from Hugging Face and runnable locally through Ollama, LM Studio or the published PyTorch/Triton/Metal implementations.

safety.note: The GPT-5.6 August Update system card reports a statistically significant regression on self-harm evaluations for the Sol tier compared with GPT-5.5 Instant, alongside enhanced protections OpenAI says it built for users under 18.

accessibility.note: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna tier is the default model for Free and Go users, with Terra and the flagship Sol tier available on paid plans; free-tier usage remains limited and dynamic.

links.label: FTC 6(b) inquiry into AI companion chatbots (2025)

products.name: Gemini (Google)
products.description: Google's consumer assistant is powerful and deeply integrated, but its consumer privacy notice is broad and settings-sensitive.

privacy.note: Google's Gemini Apps notice says chats train models when Keep Activity is on, with a default 18-month deletion window a user can shorten or extend; turning Keep Activity off stops future chats from training models and holds them for only 72 hours, and temporary chats are not used for training.

transparency.note: Google DeepMind maintains a public Gemini model-card index with 2026 cards covering architecture, evaluation and safety information.

openness.note: Gemini is closed, while Google's separate Gemma family provides open-weight models.

safety.note: Recent Gemini model cards report safety-policy evaluation, red-teaming and Frontier Safety Framework testing.

accessibility.note: Gemini is broadly available through Google's consumer products, with free and paid access paths.

links.label: FTC 6(b) inquiry into AI companion chatbots (2025)

products.name: Microsoft Copilot
products.description: A highly accessible Microsoft assistant where privacy differs sharply between consumer Copilot and enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot.

privacy.note: Consumer Copilot saves conversations by default and stores conversation activity for 18 months; Microsoft trains generative AI models on that conversation data unless a signed-in user opts out, and does not train on data from organizational accounts, unauthenticated users, under-18s, or residents of several excluded countries.

transparency.note: Microsoft publishes Copilot application-card and privacy/security documentation describing model routing, data use, permissions and review responsibilities for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

openness.note: Copilot is a closed Microsoft product, even though Microsoft also releases separate Phi open models.

safety.note: Microsoft 365 Copilot documentation describes layered safeguards for harmful content, protected-material detection and prompt-injection/jailbreak mitigation, while still requiring user review.

accessibility.note: Copilot is widely integrated across Microsoft surfaces with free, consumer and enterprise access paths.

products.name: Llama (Meta)
products.description: Meta's open-weight model family is strong for self-hosting, though licensing and training transparency are not fully open-source.

privacy.note: Running Llama locally can keep chats private, but Meta-hosted assistants and integrations have their own data policies.

transparency.note: Meta publishes model cards and license terms, but not enough training detail for full open-source reproducibility.

openness.note: Llama 4's licence lets most users download, run and fine-tune the weights royalty-free, but it is not an OSI-approved open source licence: anyone whose product passes 700 million monthly active users needs a separate licence from Meta, redistributions must display 'Built with Llama', and the licence terminates automatically if the user sues Meta over IP related to Llama.

safety.note: The Llama family includes Llama Guard and Prompt Guard models, but deployed safety depends on the app wrapper.

accessibility.note: Weights are free to access after accepting terms, but useful local deployment still requires hardware and setup.

products.name: Mistral Vibe / Le Chat
products.description: A European AI lab whose Vibe product absorbed Le Chat, paired with a strong but model-dependent open-weight release strategy.

privacy.note: Mistral's privacy policy covers Vibe/Le Chat-style inputs, outputs, usage data and feedback, with GDPR-facing controls.

transparency.note: As an EU-based provider of general-purpose AI models, Mistral has been legally required since 2 August 2025 to keep technical documentation, hold a copyright policy, and publish a sufficiently detailed public summary of training content under Article 53 of the EU AI Act; open-source releases are exempted from the documentation duties unless they carry systemic risk.

openness.note: Mistral's current model docs describe both open-weight and commercial large language models, so openness is real but model-dependent.

safety.note: Mistral has usage and privacy policies, but less public frontier-risk reporting than the most safety-documented labs.

accessibility.note: Mistral says Le Chat is now Vibe and offers a free plan, while open-weight deployment remains available for capable users.

products.name: Gemma (Google) - open weights
products.description: Google's open-weight model family is built for local, cloud and edge deployment rather than the Gemini consumer app.

privacy.note: Gemma can be run on infrastructure you control, including laptops and phones for some variants.

transparency.note: Google publishes Gemma model documentation and terms, but open weights are not the same as fully open training data.

openness.note: Gemma 4 spans four architectures (2B/4B, a dense 31B, a 26B mixture-of-experts and a 12B multimodal model) and is released under the Apache 2.0 licence, which Google says permits responsible commercial use; a separate prohibited-use policy still applies, unlike Llama's licence there is no stated user-count threshold that requires a further licence from Google.

safety.note: Gemma releases include responsible-use terms and guidance, but deployment safety depends on implementers.

accessibility.note: Gemma weights are free to download, but practical use still depends on developer tooling and hardware.

products.name: DeepSeek
products.description: A low-cost Chinese AI service with open-weight models, but hosted-service privacy and jurisdiction concerns.

privacy.note: Italy's Garante ordered an immediate, urgent limitation on DeepSeek's processing of Italian users' data on 30 January 2025, after finding the companies' response to its information request 'entirely unsatisfactory', and opened a formal investigation alongside the order.

transparency.note: The Garante's own account of its DeepSeek action says the companies initially claimed they did not operate in Italy and that EU data protection law did not apply to them, a position the Authority rejected because the web-based service was accessible to Italian users.

openness.note: DeepSeek-R1 is released under the MIT licence, and its weights can be downloaded from Hugging Face and run locally through frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang; the full 671B model needs the separate DeepSeek-V3 deployment guidance.

safety.note: The privacy policy describes safety monitoring, but public safety-framework detail is lighter than frontier lab system cards.

accessibility.note: DeepSeek is highly accessible through a free hosted product and downloadable weights.

products.name: Qwen (Alibaba)
products.description: Alibaba's Qwen family includes many open-weight releases as well as hosted/proprietary model surfaces.

privacy.note: Open-weight Qwen models can be self-hosted, but hosted Alibaba/Qwen services require trusting that provider's data handling.

transparency.note: Qwen publishes model repositories and technical reports, with clearer model access than consumer-hosted data policies.

openness.note: Qwen states its open-weight models are licensed under Apache 2.0 in the respective repositories.

safety.note: Public safety-framework detail is lighter than major frontier labs, so safe deployment depends heavily on the wrapper.

accessibility.note: Qwen weights are free to download for developers, while hosted access varies by model and platform.

products.name: NotebookLM
products.description: A Google research assistant that works from uploaded sources and is unusually explicit about not training on your notebook content by default.

privacy.note: Google says NotebookLM content is not used to directly train foundational AI models unless the user chooses to provide feedback.

transparency.note: NotebookLM documents how files, outputs and chat history are used to build the user's knowledge base.

openness.note: NotebookLM is a closed Google product, even though it may use published Gemini-family model capabilities.

safety.note: Source grounding reduces some hallucination risk, but the product still warns users to verify important outputs.

accessibility.note: NotebookLM is available through Google accounts and is easy to use for documents, notes and audio-overview workflows.

products.name: GitHub Copilot
products.description: A mainstream coding assistant deeply integrated into developer workflows, with individual-user training settings now important to check.

privacy.note: GitHub's 2026 privacy update says Copilot interaction data may be used to improve AI features, with opt-outs and enterprise protections carrying over.

transparency.note: GitHub publishes a general privacy statement and specific Copilot data-use updates, but model/provider internals are not fully inspectable.

openness.note: Copilot is a closed hosted product rather than an open-weight coding model you can self-host.

safety.note: Copilot includes coding guardrails and enterprise controls, but users remain responsible for reviewing generated code and security implications.

accessibility.note: Copilot is widely available through GitHub and major IDEs, with free, Pro, Business and Enterprise routes.

products.name: Cursor
products.description: A popular AI code editor and coding-agent environment, powerful for developers but not a local/private assistant by default.

privacy.note: Cursor says it does not use inputs or suggestions for model training except security review, user-reported feedback, or explicit user opt-in.

transparency.note: Cursor publishes privacy terms and product docs, but the coding agent and model stack are closed and provider-dependent.

openness.note: Cursor is a closed hosted/editor product that lets users choose hosted models rather than open weights they can self-host.

safety.note: Cursor supports code-aware agents and reviews, but generated code still needs human review, tests, and security scrutiny.

accessibility.note: Cursor offers free and paid routes and is packaged as a downloadable editor plus CLI/cloud-agent surfaces.

products.name: Meta AI
products.description: Meta's assistant is extremely accessible across social apps, but its default values fit is limited by Meta's ad/data ecosystem.

privacy.note: Ireland's Data Protection Commission says it pressed Meta to pause training its AI on EU/EEA adults' public Facebook and Instagram posts in June 2024, and only let training resume from 27 May 2025 after Meta added clearer transparency notices, a longer objection window, and confirmed private posts stay out of scope; Meta must report back to the DPC on how well those safeguards work.

transparency.note: Meta publishes AI-training-data explainers and privacy-center materials, but controls are region- and product-dependent.

openness.note: Meta's Llama weights improve ecosystem openness, but the Meta AI consumer assistant itself is a closed service.

safety.note: Meta has added privacy/safety features such as WhatsApp Incognito Chat, but that mode is distinct from ordinary Meta AI use.

accessibility.note: Meta says Meta AI is available across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and the web, making it one of the easiest assistants to encounter by default.

links.label: DPC statement on Meta AI training (2025)
FTC 6(b) inquiry into AI companion chatbots (2025)

products.name: Poe
products.description: A convenient multi-model chat marketplace where privacy depends on Poe, the selected model provider, and sometimes bot developers.

privacy.note: Poe says official/provider bots do not train on chats, but third-party developer bots/apps may use chats for model training.

transparency.note: Poe's privacy center distinguishes official bots, prompt bots and third-party developer bots, making the main data-flow risk visible.

openness.note: Poe aggregates proprietary and open models through a hosted interface; it is not itself an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Because Poe exposes official, user-created and third-party bots, safety behavior varies more than in a single controlled assistant.

accessibility.note: Poe is easy to use as a single interface to many models, with free and paid access paths.

products.name: Character.AI
products.description: A character-chat platform that is accessible and engaging for adults, but has removed open-ended chat for under-18s after lawsuits over teen suicides, and remains weak for privacy-sensitive users.

privacy.note: Character.AI says it retains certain user-shared data to help train and improve its AI models, with chat-training opt-out rights for EEA/UK users.

transparency.note: Character.AI publishes privacy and model-training explainers, but model behavior and companion-risk controls are not as transparent as formal system cards.

openness.note: Character.AI is a closed character-chat service, not an open-weight model family.

safety.note: Character.AI's own announcement says it removed open-ended chat with any character for users under 18 by 25 November 2025, following lawsuits after teenagers died by suicide after extended chatbot conversations; it now uses an in-house age-assurance model plus a third-party verifier (Persona) and leaves under-18s other features such as video and story creation. Companion-chat risk for adult users is unchanged by this policy.

accessibility.note: Character.AI is easy to access and designed for casual chat for adults; under-18 users lost open-ended chat access in November 2025, which narrows who the product is actually accessible to.

links.label: FTC 6(b) inquiry into AI companion chatbots (2025)

products.name: Replika
products.description: An AI companion product built for emotional conversation, with high privacy and safety sensitivity rather than everyday utility.

privacy.note: Replika's 2026 privacy policy says messages and content are used for personalized companion functionality, while conversation content is not used for marketing or third-party model training.

transparency.note: Italy's Garante fined Luka Inc. (Replika) 5 million euros on 10 April 2025, finding it had no legal basis for its data processing as of February 2023, an inadequate privacy policy, and no working age-verification either at registration or during use even though the service is meant to exclude minors; the Authority also opened a new investigation into how the underlying AI model is trained.

openness.note: Replika is a closed hosted companion service rather than an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Replika's 2026 terms restrict the service to adults, while its privacy policy warns users not to share sensitive information in companion conversations.

accessibility.note: Replika is easy to use as a mobile/web companion app, but its terms say the service is for users 18 or older.

links.label: EDPB summary of the 2025 Garante fine

products.name: Perplexity
products.description: A citation-forward answer engine that is useful for search, but consumer AI data retention is enabled by default.

privacy.note: Perplexity says Free, Pro and Max users have AI Data Retention enabled by default, with opt-out applying only to future collection.

transparency.note: Perplexity documents AI data retention and enterprise exclusions, while consumer privacy still depends on the data-retention toggle.

openness.note: Perplexity describes a multi-model answer engine, but the consumer product is a closed hosted service rather than self-hostable weights.

safety.note: Perplexity documents strong API privacy controls, but consumer safety disclosure is less extensive than frontier system-card programs.

accessibility.note: Perplexity has free consumer access, with paid tiers for higher-capacity use, but privacy settings require attention.

products.name: You.com
products.description: You.com retired its consumer chat subscriptions and now positions itself mainly as a developer and enterprise web-search API platform, though a chat sign-in still exists; most readers looking for a consumer assistant should look elsewhere.

privacy.note: You.com discloses collection of account, prompt/content, usage and telemetry data, plus LLM-provider and analytics vendors.

transparency.note: You.com publishes a detailed privacy policy and vendor categories, but consumer model routing and training behavior remain service-dependent.

openness.note: You.com is a closed hosted service/API platform rather than an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Grounded web search and source-style outputs can reduce blind-answer risk, but safety disclosure is lighter than formal model/system-card programs.

accessibility.note: You.com's site now leads with usage-based developer APIs (search, contents, answer, research) rather than a consumer chat plan; a chat sign-in remains in the site navigation, but the product is built for developers and enterprises first.

products.name: HuggingChat
products.description: A hosted chat interface from Hugging Face that emphasizes open-source and open-weight model access.

privacy.note: HuggingChat is hosted, so privacy depends on Hugging Face account/service handling; selected models can also be run elsewhere.

transparency.note: Hugging Face exposes model cards and repositories, making model choice and metadata unusually visible.

openness.note: HuggingChat is centered on selectable open-source and open-weight models hosted on Hugging Face.

safety.note: Safety varies by selected community model and guardrail layer, so the hosted chat is less consistent than a single frontier product.

accessibility.note: HuggingChat offers free hosted access to many models, subject to account and inference limits.

products.name: Kagi Assistant
products.description: A paid search-linked assistant from Kagi, built around an ad-free, user-funded privacy model.

privacy.note: Kagi documents provider-by-provider training and retention and indicates Assistant requests are not used for API model training.

transparency.note: Kagi publishes a detailed LLM privacy matrix covering provider, training and retention practices.

openness.note: Kagi Assistant is a closed paid product that routes to third-party models rather than publishing weights.

safety.note: Kagi inherits provider safeguards and search grounding, but has no major public frontier-safety framework of its own.

accessibility.note: Kagi Assistant is tied to paid Kagi plans, which improves alignment but lowers accessibility versus free assistants.

products.name: Claude Code
products.description: Anthropic's terminal coding agent is powerful and well documented, with privacy depending on account type, telemetry settings, and data-use choices.

privacy.note: Claude Code documents consumer retention choices, commercial defaults, telemetry that excludes code and file paths, and opt-out environment variables.

transparency.note: Anthropic publishes extensive Claude Code docs for settings, scopes, permissions, telemetry and enterprise controls.

openness.note: Claude Code is a closed Anthropic product using closed Claude models rather than an open-weight assistant stack.

safety.note: Claude Code benefits from Anthropic's published frontier-safety program and supports scoped settings and permission controls for tool use.

accessibility.note: Claude Code is documented for quick installation and everyday coding workflows, but meaningful use generally depends on Claude access and developer comfort.

products.name: OpenAI Codex
products.description: OpenAI's coding agent spans terminal, IDE, app, and cloud workflows, with strong accessibility but mostly closed model infrastructure.

privacy.note: OpenAI data controls let ChatGPT users turn off model improvement, while Codex can run locally via CLI or in OpenAI cloud environments.

transparency.note: OpenAI publishes Codex product documentation covering cloud delegation, CLI, IDE and app workflows.

openness.note: The Codex CLI repository is Apache-2.0 licensed, but the served coding models and cloud agent remain OpenAI-controlled.

safety.note: Codex cloud runs delegated coding tasks in isolated cloud environments and is designed for reviewable code changes.

accessibility.note: OpenAI says Codex is available across ChatGPT plans and surfaces including CLI, IDE, app and cloud, with limits varying by plan.

products.name: Gemini CLI
products.description: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini coding workflows, useful and accessible but with privacy depending heavily on authentication method and settings.

privacy.note: Gemini CLI privacy depends on authentication: individual/free use may collect prompts, answers and related code for improvement, while Standard/Enterprise and paid API paths are treated differently.

transparency.note: Google documents Gemini CLI as an open-source ReAct-style terminal agent and explains its account, quota and privacy surfaces.

openness.note: The CLI itself is open source, but it provides access to Google's Gemini models rather than an open-weight model stack.

safety.note: Gemini CLI documents sandboxing for shell commands and file changes, but sandboxing and approval choices remain important user safety settings.

accessibility.note: Gemini CLI is available from the terminal and Cloud Shell, with quotas through Gemini Code Assist editions and API-key options.

products.name: TRAE IDE / Work
products.description: A polished AI coding and work assistant from ByteDance/Spring, included as a mainstream comparison point with meaningful data-use caveats.

privacy.note: TRAE's privacy policy says the IDE collects codebase embeddings and metadata and may collect prompts, code snippets and uploaded files users provide.

transparency.note: TRAE publishes product documentation and privacy materials, but the data model is complex because codebase indexing, agent actions and workspace files are core features.

openness.note: TRAE is a proprietary IDE/workspace rather than an open-source or open-weight assistant stack.

safety.note: TRAE describes sandboxing and layered security work, but its agentic coding model still requires careful review and data-boundary choices.

accessibility.note: TRAE markets downloadable IDE and Work apps with integrated AI coding/workflow features, making it easy to try compared with self-hosted tools.

products.name: OpenCode
products.description: An open-source coding agent for terminal, desktop, and IDE use, with strong local/provider choice but user-managed safety.

privacy.note: OpenCode says it does not store code or context data, while actual prompt exposure depends on the model provider a user configures.

transparency.note: OpenCode publishes public docs and a public GitHub codebase for the coding agent.

openness.note: OpenCode describes itself as an open-source AI coding agent and supports more than 75 LLM providers, including local models.

safety.note: OpenCode provides agent and model configuration, but command execution and code-review safety depend heavily on user setup and chosen models.

accessibility.note: OpenCode is available as terminal, desktop and IDE tooling, but it is still mainly a developer tool requiring setup.

products.name: Aider
products.description: A terminal pair-programming agent that works with many LLM providers and can be paired with local models.

privacy.note: Aider can connect to local Ollama models, so privacy can be strong when users avoid remote model providers.

transparency.note: Aider publishes public docs and a public GitHub repository for its terminal coding workflow.

openness.note: Aider is an open-source tool and works with local models plus many provider APIs.

safety.note: Aider can edit code directly in a local repository, so safety depends on git review habits and the chosen model's reliability.

accessibility.note: Aider is free to install and supports free/local models, but it is a command-line developer tool.

products.name: Continue
products.description: An open-source coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and CLI users who want model choice, including local-model setups.

privacy.note: Continue documents offline use with local models and telemetry controls; prompt exposure depends on the configured model provider.

transparency.note: Continue publishes docs and source code for its IDE extensions, CLI and configuration system.

openness.note: Continue is an open-source coding agent and supports many model providers, including Ollama and self-hosted models.

safety.note: Agent behavior is user-configured through models, rules and tools, so safety depends on the chosen model and permissions setup.

accessibility.note: Continue ships as VS Code, JetBrains and CLI tooling, but meaningful setup still requires developer comfort with model/provider configuration.

products.name: Cline
products.description: An open-source agentic coding tool with strong model choice and explicit approval controls for file and terminal actions.

privacy.note: Cline supports local model providers such as Ollama and LM Studio, while hosted-provider use sends prompts to the selected provider.

transparency.note: Cline describes itself as an open coding agent and publishes its source, docs and extension/CLI surfaces.

openness.note: Cline is open source and model-agnostic, with local, BYO-key and hosted-provider paths.

safety.note: Cline's Auto Approve controls let users decide which actions can run without confirmation, making permissions a central safety choice.

accessibility.note: Cline is available across IDE, terminal and SDK surfaces, but users must understand provider costs and action approvals.

products.name: Tabby
products.description: A self-hosted code-completion and coding-assistant stack for teams that want Copilot-style help without sending code to a SaaS assistant.

privacy.note: Tabby is positioned as self-hosted and on-premises, so code and prompts can stay inside the user's own infrastructure.

transparency.note: Tabby publishes public documentation and source for its open-source coding assistant.

openness.note: Tabby describes itself as an open-source, self-hosted AI coding assistant and Copilot alternative.

safety.note: Self-hosting improves data boundaries, but generated code and completions still require review and model governance by the deploying team.

accessibility.note: Tabby is powerful for privacy-sensitive teams, but setup requires server/GPU or infrastructure comfort.

products.name: Kilo Code
products.description: An open-source coding agent spanning IDE, CLI and cloud workflows, notable for broad model choice and local-model support.

privacy.note: Kilo documents local-model support through Ollama, LM Studio and Atomic Chat, where code and data can stay on the user's machine.

transparency.note: Kilo publishes its source and describes its pricing/model routing claims publicly.

openness.note: Kilo describes itself as an open-source AI coding agent with BYO keys, local models and zero AI inference markup.

safety.note: Kilo supports multiple agent modes and broad tool access, so safety depends on permissions, review habits and provider choices.

accessibility.note: Kilo covers VS Code, JetBrains, CLI and cloud agent surfaces, making it easier to start than a purely self-hosted stack.

products.name: CodeRabbit
products.description: An AI code-review and planning platform for pull requests, IDEs, CLI and Slack, useful for teams adopting coding agents but important to weigh for repository-access risk.

privacy.note: CodeRabbit says review-improvement storage can be opted out of and mainly uses vector embeddings, but repository review still involves hosted processing.

transparency.note: CodeRabbit publishes docs for PR review, planning, Slack agent, CLI and IDE review workflows.

openness.note: CodeRabbit is a closed hosted review platform rather than an open-source or open-weight coding assistant.

safety.note: CodeRabbit's 2026 changelog says SkillSpector is enabled by default to detect security risks in AI-agent and MCP configuration, but repository-access tools still require permission caution.

accessibility.note: CodeRabbit supports GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket review plus IDE, CLI and Slack surfaces.

products.name: Zed AI
products.description: A fast open-source editor with built-in AI features, local/model-provider choice, and unusually direct privacy commitments.

privacy.note: Zed's AI privacy docs explain trust boundaries, and its privacy policy says providers are not allowed to train on user data.

transparency.note: Zed publishes AI docs for model access, privacy and agent behavior, plus a public editor codebase.

openness.note: Zed is open source and compatible with hosted models, provider API access, gateways and local models.

safety.note: Zed Agent uses tool profiles and permission controls for file edits, terminal commands and MCP tools.

accessibility.note: Zed integrates AI directly into a code editor, but meaningful use still depends on model access and developer workflow comfort.

products.name: Msty Studio
products.description: A local-first AI workspace for chatting with local and hosted models while keeping ordinary chat data on the user's device by default.

privacy.note: Msty says Studio, App and Claw data are stored locally, never transmitted to its servers, and no analytics or telemetry are collected.

transparency.note: Msty publishes a privacy-first explanation distinguishing local storage from cloud-provider connections.

openness.note: Msty supports local models through Ollama, MLX and llama.cpp, though the product itself is a managed app rather than a fully open assistant stack.

safety.note: Local models improve data control but leave hallucination, context limits and guardrail quality to the chosen model and user workflow.

accessibility.note: Msty Studio provides desktop and web workflows, local and online model management, and a free starting path.

products.name: OpenRouter
products.description: A multi-model API router that gives developers model choice, but shifts privacy literacy onto provider selection and retention settings.

privacy.note: OpenRouter offers Zero Data Retention routing controls, but provider logging and retention policies vary by selected provider.

transparency.note: OpenRouter documents provider logging, retention and routing controls so users can choose providers more deliberately.

openness.note: OpenRouter is not an open-weight model itself, but it exposes one API for hundreds of models and providers.

safety.note: Safety behavior depends on the routed model and provider; OpenRouter mainly supplies routing, fallbacks and provider controls.

accessibility.note: OpenRouter provides a unified API with hundreds of models through a single endpoint, lowering switching costs for developers.

products.name: v0 by Vercel
products.description: A hosted AI interface and app builder for React/Next.js projects, powerful for prototyping but important to read for training and publish controls.

privacy.note: v0's FAQ says user prompts/content may be used to improve products unless covered by enterprise or opt-out settings.

transparency.note: v0 documents training, deletion, security and enterprise controls in public docs and policy pages.

openness.note: v0 is a closed hosted Vercel product, though generated code can be edited, synced and deployed.

safety.note: v0 documents sandboxed execution, code analysis, environment-variable checks and enterprise security controls.

accessibility.note: v0 offers a free plan, visual editing, GitHub sync and one-click deployment, with usage limits by plan.

products.name: Bolt
products.description: A browser-based AI app builder that lowers the barrier to full-stack prototypes, but generated apps and data settings still need careful review.

privacy.note: StackBlitz's privacy policy says AI inputs/outputs may be used to improve services on aggregated, anonymized or de-identified data, with controls depending on plan.

transparency.note: Bolt's help center and StackBlitz policies explain the hosted builder and privacy terms, but training controls are plan-dependent.

openness.note: Bolt has an open-source codebase reference, but the main product is a hosted AI app builder tied to StackBlitz infrastructure.

safety.note: Bolt runs browser development environments through WebContainers, but AI-generated app code still needs human security review before production.

accessibility.note: Bolt is built for prompt-to-app creation in the browser and offers a free starting plan.

products.name: Lovable
products.description: A popular prompt-to-app builder whose biggest literacy issue is understanding project visibility, training opt-outs and app security before publishing.

privacy.note: Lovable's privacy policy says raw or identifiable personal data is not used for training, while customer-data opt-out requires contact or Business controls.

transparency.note: Lovable documents training-data controls, project access and published-website access as separate concepts.

openness.note: Lovable generates editable applications, but the builder itself is a closed hosted service rather than an open-weight assistant.

safety.note: Lovable documents project access, publishing controls and security guidance, but users still own app-level privacy and security decisions.

accessibility.note: Lovable is designed as a prompt-driven app builder with broad onboarding and documentation for non-specialist builders.

products.name: Notion AI
products.description: A workspace assistant embedded in Notion, useful for notes and knowledge work with stronger enterprise privacy than many consumer assistants.

privacy.note: Notion says Customer Data is not used to train Notion or subprocessor models by default and that AI honors existing permissions.

transparency.note: Notion publishes dedicated AI security and privacy practices explaining subprocessors, permissions and retention.

openness.note: Notion AI is a closed workspace product that uses third-party AI subprocessors rather than open weights.

safety.note: Notion AI honors workspace permissions and includes SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 scope, but outputs still require user review.

accessibility.note: Notion AI is easy for existing Notion users and included in Business and Enterprise plans, with limited trial usage elsewhere.

products.name: Grammarly AI
products.description: A mainstream writing assistant with strong accessibility, but individual-user training defaults deserve close attention.

privacy.note: Grammarly says Product Improvement and Training is on by default for individual Free, Premium and single-user Pro accounts, with opt-out controls.

transparency.note: Grammarly publishes support documentation distinguishing individual and organization training controls.

openness.note: Grammarly AI is a closed writing assistant and browser/app integration rather than an open-weight model.

safety.note: Grammarly says it filters generative AI and language suggestions for harmful content such as hate speech.

accessibility.note: Grammarly's AI writing features are widely available across browser, app and writing surfaces, including free and paid paths.

products.name: Slack AI
products.description: A workplace assistant for search, summaries and Slackbot features, with unusually explicit enterprise data-boundary promises.

privacy.note: Slack says it will not use Customer Data to train generative AI models without affirmative opt-in consent and keeps data in Slack's trust boundary.

transparency.note: Slack publishes AI privacy principles and security documentation for native AI features.

openness.note: Slack AI is a closed Salesforce/Slack workplace product using third-party LLMs rather than downloadable weights.

safety.note: Slack documents AI guardrails including content thresholds, prompt-injection risk reduction, URL filtering and output validation.

accessibility.note: Slack AI is useful inside existing Slack workspaces, but it is gated by Slack plans and admin configuration.

products.name: Zoom AI Companion / ZoomMate
products.description: Zoom's meeting and workplace assistant helps summarize, search and create follow-up work, with strong no-training commitments but sensitive-meeting caveats.

privacy.note: Zoom says it does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or similar customer content to train Zoom or third-party AI models.

transparency.note: Zoom documents how AI features process meeting data, third-party model use, retention and admin controls.

openness.note: ZoomMate is a closed Zoom product using Zoom and third-party models rather than open weights.

safety.note: Zoom provides admin controls and model-provider retention commitments, but meeting assistants still create shareable records from sensitive conversations.

accessibility.note: ZoomMate Basic includes limited AI features on Workplace Basic, while fuller agentic features require paid AI plans.

products.name: Elicit
products.description: A research-focused assistant for finding, summarizing and extracting information from scientific literature.

privacy.note: Elicit publishes a privacy policy for its site and services, but it is still a hosted research platform that collects account and usage information.

transparency.note: Elicit clearly describes its literature-search, report-generation and extraction workflows and publishes trust resources.

openness.note: Elicit is a closed hosted research assistant rather than an open-weight or self-hosted model.

safety.note: Elicit is source-grounded in academic papers and reports testing/evaluation examples, but scientific summaries still need expert checking.

accessibility.note: Elicit offers a public research workflow and is designed for ordinary literature-review use, though heavy use is plan-limited.

products.name: Consensus
products.description: An academic search assistant that emphasizes evidence-backed answers rather than open-ended chatbot conversation.

privacy.note: Consensus says user and behavior data is anonymized and that it logs anonymized query text to improve search.

transparency.note: Consensus publishes help-center security documentation and a privacy policy for its research-search product.

openness.note: Consensus is a closed hosted search assistant rather than an open-weight or self-hostable model.

safety.note: Consensus is constrained around academic-search queries, which reduces general chatbot risk but does not replace reading the underlying studies.

accessibility.note: Consensus is easy to use as a public research search tool, with deeper workflows depending on account and plan.

products.name: Jasper
products.description: A marketing-oriented AI agent platform with enterprise security claims and a narrower values fit for users avoiding persuasion tooling.

privacy.note: Jasper says it does not use customer data to train AI models and lists SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA, PCI and DPA controls.

transparency.note: Jasper publishes security, privacy, pricing and responsible-AI pages, though model internals remain closed.

openness.note: Jasper is a closed marketing AI platform and agent workspace rather than an open-weight model users can self-host.

safety.note: Jasper says internal AI usage standards emphasize transparency, accountability, quality, privacy and human review for generated content.

accessibility.note: Jasper offers trials and paid business workflows, but is aimed mainly at marketing teams rather than general consumers.

products.name: Writer / Palmyra
products.description: An enterprise AI platform built around Writer's Palmyra models, governance, and agent workflows.

privacy.note: Writer says Palmyra LLMs do not store customer data for training and also offers self-hosted LLM options.

transparency.note: Writer publishes trust, governance and model-selection documentation for Palmyra and external model use.

openness.note: Writer's hosted platform is proprietary, though its materials describe some Palmyra models as available through external model and download paths.

safety.note: Writer emphasizes enterprise governance features such as guardrails, granular permissions, approval flows and decision traces.

accessibility.note: Writer is mainly an enterprise platform, so ordinary consumer accessibility is lower than free chat assistants.

products.name: Phi (Microsoft) - open small models
products.description: Microsoft's small open model family is built for edge and on-device deployment with strong model-card documentation.

privacy.note: Phi models can be deployed locally, at the edge, or in cloud environments you control.

transparency.note: Microsoft publishes detailed Phi model cards with training data, evaluation and safety sections.

openness.note: Phi is available through Hugging Face, Ollama and Microsoft Foundry as an open model family.

safety.note: Phi-4's model card describes safety post-training, safety evaluation and red-teaming.

accessibility.note: Phi is free through common developer channels, but still requires model tooling or cloud deployment know-how.

products.name: Grok (xAI)
products.description: xAI's assistant is accessible and partly open-weight historically, but privacy and safety are weaker fits for cautious users.

privacy.note: xAI says it may use Grok prompts, searches, uploaded materials and responses to train models unless users opt out or use Private Chat.

transparency.note: Ireland's Data Protection Commission used untested High Court powers for the first time in August 2024 to make X suspend processing EU/EEA users' public posts collected between 7 May and 1 August 2024 for training Grok; the proceedings were struck out in September 2024 after X gave a permanent undertaking to keep to those terms.

openness.note: xAI released Grok-1 weights and architecture under Apache 2.0, but that release is an older base model, not the current assistant.

safety.note: xAI's own FAQ says user-selected modes can produce coarse, suggestive, violent or offensive content, so safety fit is limited.

accessibility.note: Grok has limited free and paid consumer access on mobile, web and X depending on location.

links.label: FTC 6(b) inquiry into AI companion chatbots (2025)

products.name: Cohere Command
products.description: An enterprise-oriented model family with strong deployment controls and some open-weight research releases.

privacy.note: Cohere says it deletes logged SaaS prompts and generations after 30 days by default, lets customers opt out of training use through a Data Controls toggle in dashboard settings, and offers zero-data-retention for enterprise customers who meet additional usage commitments.

transparency.note: Cohere publishes model documentation and enterprise data commitments, but consumer-style disclosure is less relevant.

openness.note: Cohere Labs has open-weight research releases such as Command A, but core Command products remain enterprise-oriented.

safety.note: Cohere positions Command for enterprise use with data controls, misuse monitoring and usage-policy enforcement, while public frontier-risk reporting remains more limited.

accessibility.note: Cohere is developer and enterprise oriented, so ordinary consumer accessibility is lower than free chat assistants.

products.name: Canva AI / Magic Studio
products.description: A mainstream design-and-content assistant embedded in Canva, useful for quick visuals but governed by broad platform AI terms and partner-model use.

privacy.note: Canva says AI inputs may be shared with technology partners and privacy settings control whether Canva and partners may use data to improve AI services.

transparency.note: Canva publishes dedicated AI Product Terms plus a Trust Centre / Canva Shield explanation for AI controls.

openness.note: Canva AI is a closed hosted product suite, with no downloadable model weights or self-hosting path.

safety.note: Canva's AI terms prohibit deceptive, harmful and rights-violating uses and say AI outputs may carry provenance/C2PA metadata.

accessibility.note: Canva AI is broadly available inside a popular freemium design platform, though quotas and some controls vary by plan.

products.name: Adobe Firefly
products.description: Adobe's creative generative-AI family, notable for commercial-safety positioning, Content Credentials, and a more rights-aware training story.

privacy.note: Adobe says Firefly is not trained on Creative Cloud subscribers' personal content or customer content.

transparency.note: Adobe explains Firefly's licensed/public-domain training approach and Content Authenticity Initiative participation.

openness.note: Firefly models are proprietary hosted Adobe models rather than open weights users can inspect or self-host.

safety.note: Adobe says Firefly uses licensed/public-domain training, content safeguards and automatic Content Credentials for certain Firefly exports.

accessibility.note: Firefly is available as a standalone web app and through Adobe products, with plan and generative-credit limits.

products.name: Midjourney
products.description: A widely used image and video generator with strong creative appeal but public-by-default community norms and closed models.

privacy.note: Midjourney's terms say content is publicly viewable and remixable by default unless paid Stealth mode or private spaces apply.

transparency.note: Midjourney publishes privacy, terms and community rules, but offers limited model-card or training-data transparency.

openness.note: Midjourney is a closed hosted generation service with no open weights or self-hosting path.

safety.note: Midjourney has PG-13 community guidelines and bans deceptive, infringing, adult, gore and election-influence uses, but also warns outputs are AI-generated and not guaranteed.

accessibility.note: Midjourney is consumer-facing and popular, but meaningful private use and higher capacity require paid plans.

products.name: Runway
products.description: A powerful creative-video platform, useful for AI filmmaking and editing but weaker for privacy because standard terms permit training on inputs and outputs.

privacy.note: Runway's terms say inputs and outputs may be used to train and improve its AI models, products and services.

transparency.note: Runway publishes terms, privacy and a trust/safety help section, but gives limited public training-data or model-card detail.

openness.note: Runway is a proprietary hosted creative-video service with no open model weights or self-hosting route.

safety.note: Runway reserves the right to review or monitor inputs and outputs and prohibits rights-violating, deceptive and harmful content, but output risks remain user-managed.

accessibility.note: Runway is available through a web creative suite, but heavier video-generation use is constrained by paid plans and credits.

products.name: ElevenLabs
products.description: A synthetic-voice and audio platform with strong product reach and visible safety work, but sensitive biometric/voice-data tradeoffs.

privacy.note: ElevenLabs says it may process personal data including audio, text, video and metadata to train or improve AI models, with disassociation practices and applicable rights.

transparency.note: ElevenLabs publishes a privacy policy, safety page and trust center, including voice-data and moderation disclosures.

openness.note: ElevenLabs' voice and audio models are proprietary hosted services rather than open weights users can self-host.

safety.note: ElevenLabs describes safeguards for abuse prevention, traceability, content provenance and misuse response for synthetic audio.

accessibility.note: ElevenLabs offers broad web/API access for voice, speech and audio tools, including consumer and business plans.

products.name: Descript / Underlord
products.description: An AI audio/video editing suite and assistant for podcasts, screen recordings and social clips, with relatively explicit data-sharing controls.

privacy.note: Descript says AI subprocessors cannot train on user data and in-house AI training uses clear opt-in data sharing; enterprise data sharing is disabled by default.

transparency.note: Descript publishes account-data/privacy help, security pages and an assurance profile with SOC 2/GDPR/CCPA references.

openness.note: Descript and Underlord are proprietary hosted/desktop tools rather than open-weight or self-hostable AI assistants.

safety.note: Descript's AI tools are designed for human-edited media workflows, but generated edits still require creator review and consent awareness.

accessibility.note: Descript provides a consumer-friendly editor with AI tools, while heavier use and team controls depend on paid plans.

products.name: Otter.ai
products.description: A popular meeting transcription and summarization assistant; useful, but meeting bots carry special consent and sensitive-conversation risks.

privacy.note: Otter says it uses de-identified user data to train its models and requires users to obtain consent before recording and transcribing conversations.

transparency.note: Otter publishes a privacy/security page describing recording, sharing, deletion, subprocessors, law-enforcement handling and security controls.

openness.note: Otter is a proprietary hosted transcription and meeting-agent service, not an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Otter emphasizes participant consent and private conversation controls, but automated meeting recording still requires careful user governance.

accessibility.note: Otter offers web, desktop, mobile and meeting integrations with free and paid access paths.

products.name: Fathom AI Notetaker
products.description: A meeting recorder and AI summarizer with a generous free tier and clearer model-training disclosures than many meeting assistants.

privacy.note: Fathom says AI subprocessors cannot train on user data, while Fathom may use de-identified meeting content to train in-house models unless users opt out.

transparency.note: Fathom publishes security FAQs, privacy terms and details on meeting-content collection, deletion, opt-out and subprocessors.

openness.note: Fathom is a proprietary hosted meeting notetaker rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Fathom warns users that some states/countries require all-party consent before recording meetings and places consent responsibility on users.

accessibility.note: Fathom offers a free individual meeting notetaker and paid team controls, making it unusually accessible in the category.

products.name: Fireflies.ai
products.description: A meeting transcription, summary and workflow assistant with strong security marketing and enterprise controls, but still a sensitive meeting-data surface.

privacy.note: Fireflies says users own their data, it does not train on meeting data by default, and enterprise options include private storage and retention controls.

transparency.note: Fireflies publishes security, privacy, trust-center and FAQ materials for meeting transcripts and recordings.

openness.note: Fireflies is a proprietary hosted meeting assistant, not an open-source or self-hostable tool.

safety.note: Fireflies documents admin controls, limited data access, encryption and meeting-data ownership, but meeting capture remains consent-sensitive.

accessibility.note: Fireflies integrates with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, email, chat and CRM workflows, with free and paid plans.

products.name: Granola
products.description: A desktop/iPhone meeting-note assistant that avoids a visible meeting bot and stores notes rather than recordings, but trains on anonymized user data unless opted out.

privacy.note: Granola says third-party AI providers cannot train on user data, but Granola trains on anonymized data unless users opt out; enterprise training is off by default.

transparency.note: Granola's security page explains local audio capture, model training, storage, sharing and deletion basics in unusually plain language.

openness.note: Granola is a proprietary meeting-notes app rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Granola says users manually start meetings and it does not store recordings, but no-bot meeting notes still require social and legal consent judgment.

accessibility.note: Granola works with common meeting platforms via desktop and iPhone apps, with business controls available for teams.

products.name: Synthesia
products.description: An enterprise-friendly AI avatar/video platform with explicit consent, governance and customer-data boundaries.

privacy.note: Synthesia says it does not use customer inputs or outputs to pre-train its AI components, except customer-instructed fine-tuning under agreement.

transparency.note: Synthesia publishes AI governance practices aligned to ISO/IEC 42001, plus trust-center material for security and AI-assurance controls.

openness.note: Synthesia is a proprietary hosted avatar/video service, not an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Synthesia's responsible-AI materials describe consent, content moderation, misuse reporting and trust-and-safety controls for AI avatars and video.

accessibility.note: Synthesia offers a free creation path but is primarily positioned for enterprise video, training and localization teams.

products.name: HeyGen
products.description: A consumer-and-enterprise AI avatar/video platform with visible compliance claims and mixed privacy depending on enterprise status.

privacy.note: HeyGen says enterprise customer data is not used for training, while non-enterprise customer data may be used unless users opt out.

transparency.note: HeyGen publishes trust/safety, privacy and security pages with subprocessor, compliance and moderation disclosures.

openness.note: HeyGen is a proprietary hosted avatar/video service rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: HeyGen describes automated moderation, enforcement review, trust-and-safety staffing, and compliance with SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA and EU AI Act obligations.

accessibility.note: HeyGen offers free-start AI video tools and many creator workflows, while enterprise governance requires higher-tier plans.

products.name: Roo Code
products.description: An open-source VS Code coding-agent extension with multi-agent workflows and user-selected model providers.

privacy.note: Roo Code is open source and model-provider agnostic, so prompt privacy depends on the provider, API keys and local configuration a user chooses.

transparency.note: The docs and repository describe agent modes, tool use, MCP support, settings and extension behavior publicly.

openness.note: The Roo Code repository is public and licensed Apache-2.0.

safety.note: Roo Code can run agentic coding workflows inside an editor, so users still need review, tool limits and secrets hygiene.

accessibility.note: Roo Code works inside VS Code-compatible environments and supports multiple providers, but setup is still developer-oriented.

products.name: OpenHands
products.description: An open-source platform for cloud or self-hosted software-development agents that can plan, edit and run code.

privacy.note: OpenHands can be self-hosted or run as a hosted agent platform, so privacy depends on deployment and connected repositories/secrets.

transparency.note: OpenHands describes its platform, SDK and cloud coding agent architecture publicly, with source code available on GitHub.

openness.note: The OpenHands project is public on GitHub and presents itself as an open-source agent platform for software development.

safety.note: OpenHands agents can execute real engineering work across codebases, so review, sandboxing and secret isolation matter.

accessibility.note: OpenHands offers an agent platform and SDK, but it is aimed at software teams rather than casual AI users.

products.name: mini-SWE-agent
products.description: A deliberately small open-source command-line coding agent for solving GitHub issues and experimenting with SWE-bench style workflows.

privacy.note: mini-SWE-agent is local/open source, but it connects to a user-selected language model provider and can operate on local repositories.

transparency.note: The project advertises a radically small implementation and documents its CLI-oriented agent design publicly.

openness.note: mini-SWE-agent is public on GitHub under the MIT license.

safety.note: The tool is designed to solve issues and use command-line workflows, so it should be run in reviewed, sandboxed development contexts.

accessibility.note: The small CLI design is attractive for technical users, but it is less accessible than hosted consumer assistants.

products.name: goose
products.description: An open-source desktop, CLI and API agent for coding, research, writing, automation and local task execution.

privacy.note: goose runs on a user's machine and connects to selected LLM providers, so prompt privacy depends on local setup and provider choice.

transparency.note: The docs describe goose as a general-purpose agent with desktop, CLI and API surfaces, and the repository is public.

openness.note: goose is an open-source agent project that moved from Block to the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation.

safety.note: goose can automate local computer tasks through extensions and tools, so users need clear permissions and review boundaries.

accessibility.note: goose provides desktop, CLI and API options across operating systems, though it is still a technical agent tool.

products.name: Open Interpreter
products.description: An open-source local coding/computer agent route for letting language models run code and interact with a user's machine.

privacy.note: Open Interpreter is open source and can run locally, but connected model providers may still receive prompts and outputs.

transparency.note: The repository documents harness emulation, model provider choices and the local coding-agent approach.

openness.note: Open Interpreter is public on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 license.

safety.note: Because it gives models code and shell execution capabilities, safe use depends on sandboxing and explicit user review.

accessibility.note: The project is powerful for technical users, but local setup and execution-risk management raise the difficulty floor.

products.name: Dify
products.description: An open-source platform for building AI workflows, RAG apps, agents and model-powered products.

privacy.note: Dify can be self-hosted or used as a hosted platform, so privacy depends on deployment, connected models and data-store configuration.

transparency.note: The repository documents Dify's workflow, RAG, agent, model-management and observability features publicly.

openness.note: Dify describes itself as an open-source LLM app development platform and publishes its core code on GitHub.

safety.note: Dify includes observability and app-building controls, but AI workflow builders still require governance around prompts, tools and data sources.

accessibility.note: Dify's visual workflow builder lowers the barrier for creating AI apps, though production use remains technical.

products.name: Flowise
products.description: An open-source low-code builder for LLM apps, chatbots, RAG systems and agentic workflows.

privacy.note: Flowise can be self-hosted, but privacy and data exposure depend on deployment, authentication and connected model/vector services.
