transparency.note: Flowise publicly documents its visual building blocks for agents, chatflows and LLM-powered workflows.

openness.note: Flowise is public on GitHub and describes itself as an open-source visual AI agent builder.

safety.note: Flowise's power comes from connecting tools and workflows; exposed or outdated instances can create significant security risk.

accessibility.note: The visual builder makes LLM app construction easier than code-only frameworks, but safe hosting still needs technical judgment.

products.name: Langflow
products.description: An open-source visual framework for building AI applications, agents, MCP tools and RAG workflows.

privacy.note: Langflow is open source and can be self-hosted, while hosted use depends on platform and connected model providers.

transparency.note: Langflow documentation describes the visual editor, agent support, MCP support and model/vector-store flexibility.

openness.note: Langflow's public GitHub repository describes it as completely open source.

safety.note: Agent and MCP workflows need governance around tools, credentials and data sources even when the builder is open source.

accessibility.note: Langflow's visual editor supports low-code prototyping for AI applications, agents and RAG workflows.

products.name: Open SWE
products.description: An open-source asynchronous coding-agent framework for internal software engineering agents that plan, code, test and open pull requests.

privacy.note: Open SWE is designed for GitHub-connected asynchronous coding agents, so repository and issue privacy depend on deployment and GitHub/model configuration.

transparency.note: LangChain publicly explains Open SWE's architecture and purpose as an internal coding-agent framework.

openness.note: LangChain presents Open SWE as an open-source framework and links the public repository.

safety.note: The framework is explicitly for agents that work on codebases and open pull requests, so safe use requires review and access boundaries.

accessibility.note: Open SWE is a framework for technical teams rather than a consumer coding assistant.

products.name: Qodo
products.description: A proprietary AI code review and quality platform focused on reviewing, testing and governing code changes.

privacy.note: Qodo's privacy policy describes processing personal information through its website and platform, including service and product data.

transparency.note: Qodo publishes product, documentation and privacy pages explaining its AI code review and agentic quality workflows.

openness.note: Qodo is a proprietary code-review service rather than an open-source/self-hostable coding agent.

safety.note: Qodo is review-first and emphasizes catching bugs, security issues and governance problems rather than simply generating more code.

accessibility.note: Qodo offers IDE, pull request and CLI workflows, but fuller organizational value is aimed at engineering teams.

products.name: Gamma
products.description: A hosted AI presentation and document-generation tool with strong accessibility and weaker openness.

privacy.note: Gamma's privacy policy describes collection and processing of personal information across its online service and marketing activities.

transparency.note: Gamma publishes privacy documentation and a help article explaining privacy, encryption, user controls and AI-related data practices.

openness.note: Gamma is a proprietary hosted presentation service rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Gamma is mostly a productivity and presentation generator, but users still need to verify sources and protect private documents.

accessibility.note: Gamma is easy to start with and designed around quickly creating presentations, webpages and documents.

products.name: Napkin AI
products.description: A hosted tool for turning text into diagrams, visuals and presentation-ready explainers.

privacy.note: Napkin's privacy policy describes personal-information processing for its services and account workflows.

transparency.note: Napkin's pricing FAQ says users can opt out of data sharing for model training and that AI subprocessors are contractually restricted from training on customer data.

openness.note: Napkin AI is a proprietary hosted visual-generation service rather than an open-source/self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Napkin is lower risk than code-executing agents, but generated diagrams still need accuracy and source checks before publication.

accessibility.note: Napkin is designed to create professional visuals from text without requiring design skill.

products.name: Ideogram
products.description: A hosted image-generation platform with strong usability and limited openness/training transparency.

privacy.note: Ideogram publishes privacy/trust resources, but hosted image-generation workflows still involve account and generated-content data.

transparency.note: Ideogram publishes usage policies and a trust center, but model weights and training datasets are not open.

openness.note: Ideogram is a proprietary hosted image-generation service rather than an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Ideogram publishes usage policies for responsible service use and content restrictions.

accessibility.note: Ideogram is a consumer-accessible image generator with web and app workflows.

products.name: Leonardo.Ai
products.description: A hosted AI image and video generator with broad creator tooling and public/private asset tradeoffs.

privacy.note: Leonardo.Ai's privacy policy covers the cloud AI platform, website, apps, plug-ins and related services.

transparency.note: Leonardo explains plan differences around generated asset ownership and public/private image handling.

openness.note: Leonardo.Ai is a proprietary hosted platform rather than an open-source or open-weight assistant.

safety.note: Generated assets on free/public settings can be visible and reusable, so commercial and privacy-sensitive work needs plan and visibility checks.

accessibility.note: Leonardo offers a mobile/web AI image and video generator with free-plan access and many creator workflows.

products.name: Krea
products.description: A hosted creative AI suite for generating and editing images, video and 3D assets.

privacy.note: Krea's enterprise page says customer data is not used to train or improve models for enterprise customers.

transparency.note: Krea publishes public product and enterprise privacy/security claims, but not open weights or full model training data.

openness.note: Krea is a proprietary hosted creative AI suite rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Krea is easier than agentic code tools, but generated image/video work still requires rights, likeness and publication judgment.

accessibility.note: Krea advertises free access for generating, enhancing and editing images, video and 3D meshes.

products.name: Luma Dream Machine
products.description: A hosted creative AI platform for text/image-to-video generation and broader visual agent workflows.

privacy.note: Luma's privacy policy says it collects account data, communications, uploaded user content and other service-use information.

transparency.note: Luma publishes service and privacy pages, but Dream Machine models and training data are not open.

openness.note: Dream Machine is a proprietary hosted creative AI service rather than an open-weight or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Luma creative agents can generate and iterate visual content, so users need rights, likeness and publication review.

accessibility.note: Dream Machine is a web-accessible creative generation interface, though sustained generation depends on plan and credits.

products.name: Pika
products.description: A hosted AI video platform for prompt, image and effect-driven short-form video creation.

privacy.note: Pika's privacy policy says user contributions are made at the user's own risk and may involve profile privacy settings.

transparency.note: Pika publishes privacy and terms pages, but does not provide open model weights or full training-data transparency.

openness.note: Pika is a proprietary hosted AI video service rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Pika's terms put responsibility on users for how AI selves and generated content are instructed and shared.

accessibility.note: Pika is designed for easy short-form video generation from prompts, images and effects.

products.name: Suno
products.description: A mainstream hosted AI music generator with easy access and significant creator-rights/copyright caution.

privacy.note: Suno's privacy notice explains collection, use, sharing, storage and choices around service information.

transparency.note: Suno publishes privacy and terms pages, but it does not provide open weights or full training-data transparency.

openness.note: Suno is a proprietary hosted music-generation service rather than an open-source or self-hostable assistant.

safety.note: Suno's terms require users to follow service rules and manage legal responsibility for their use of generated music.

accessibility.note: Suno is built around easy prompt-to-song creation with a consumer web interface.

products.name: SOUNDRAW
products.description: A hosted AI music generator that emphasizes royalty-free output and in-house training material.

privacy.note: SOUNDRAW publishes GDPR and privacy materials for handling user and account data.

transparency.note: SOUNDRAW says its algorithm is based on in-house musicians' input rather than scraped data.

openness.note: SOUNDRAW is a proprietary hosted music-generation service rather than open source or open-weight.

safety.note: SOUNDRAW's license page directly addresses royalty-free use and training-data claims, which reduces but does not eliminate creator-rights due diligence.

accessibility.note: SOUNDRAW is designed to make AI-generated royalty-free beats and music accessible through a web service.
